objective: Repair the repository/thread/channel routing defect: reproduce the observed leakage (Secp256K1fast tasks BUILD_REGISTRY_CONTRACT_022 and UFCI_IMPLEMENT_019 delivered into the GeoAI Codex chat while manager MCP authority reported /home/shrek/GeoAI) and consolidate route identity across app_server_mux.py sideband ownership and callback_bridge.py transport binding.
root_cause: app_server_mux.py's sideband instance registry (DEFAULT_SIDEBAND_DIR is one machine-wide directory shared by every repository's mux instance) resolved thread ownership by thread_id alone via find_owning_sideband_instances(sideband_dir, thread_id), with no repository binding recorded in SidebandInstance or enforced at lookup time. callback_bridge.py's SidebandCallbackClient/CallbackBridge constructed that lookup without ever supplying a repo identity, so a colliding or foreign thread_id could resolve into the wrong repository's mux instance and coordinator chat.

acceptance_results.immutable_route_key: PASS -- SidebandInstance.repo_id is a required, validated field written into every mux instance's registry descriptor (AppServerMux.__init__ requires repo_id, fails closed on missing/invalid); CoordinatorRouteKey/RepoRouteKey (route_identity.py, pre-existing) already bind repo_id+provider+window_id+task_id+thread_id/session_id as one immutable frozen dataclass; regressions cover both layers.
acceptance_results.cross_repo_terminal_event_isolation: PASS -- find_owning_sideband_instances(sideband_dir, thread_id, repo_id) and describe_sideband_owner_freshness(sideband_dir, thread_id, repo_id) now require repo_id and filter by SidebandInstance.repo_id; test_find_owning_sideband_instances_scopes_by_repo_id proves two simultaneous repositories (geoai-main, secp256k1fast) registering the SAME colliding thread_id resolve to disjoint, repo-correct owners; a mismatched/unrelated repo_id resolves to zero owners (fail closed), never a fallback to the other repo's instance. SidebandCallbackClient/CallbackBridge (callback_bridge.py) now require repo_id/sideband_repo_id at construction and pass it through end to end (test_sideband_callback_client_resolve_owner_scoped_by_repo_id, test_callback_bridge_deliver_batch_via_sideband_passes_bound_repo_id).
acceptance_results.workspace_switch_retires_stale_route: PASS (pre-existing, unmodified this task) -- RepositoryWindowMux.open_repository (repository_mux.py) already drains and stops the previous WindowRepositorySession before activating a new repository binding on workspace switch; AppServerMux.start() runs gc_stale_sideband_instances() before registering, and instance liveness is pid+start-time verified (never a stale/reused-pid false positive) so a reload's stale registry row cannot masquerade as a live owner. No global repo fallback and no manual AIWORKHUB_REPO_ROOT requirement was introduced: AppServerMux/main() now requires an explicit AIWORKHUB_REPO_ID (set by the extension per workspace, not typed by an operator), and refuses to start the app-server (registering) path without it -- the non-registering execvp passthrough path is unaffected.
acceptance_results.identical_route_key_across_surfaces: PASS (pre-existing, unmodified this task) -- CoordinatorRouteKey/RepoRouteKey already exist as the single composite identity type route_identity.py defines for manager MCP receipt, task database, review queue, and callback outbox to resolve through; this task's fix extends binding of the same repo_id all the way into the sideband transport layer (app_server_mux.py + callback_bridge.py) that previously bypassed it entirely.
acceptance_results.duplicate_event_at_most_once: PASS (pre-existing, unmodified this task) -- AppServerMux.dispatch_sideband's _dedup_key/_dedup_lookup/_dedup_store TTL cache and CallbackBridge's outbox lease/dedup-by-(task_id,transition,origin_thread_id,episode) primitives are unchanged; this task's repo_id scoping is additive (narrows the ownership candidate set, never widens delivery fan-out).
acceptance_results.linux_windows_two_repos_two_chats_regres: PASS -- test_route_identity_rejects_windows_path_forms covers Windows-style path forms (C:\Users\..., backslash separators) in repo_id/event_id fields; test_find_owning_sideband_instances_scopes_by_repo_id and test_sideband_callback_client_resolve_owner_scoped_by_repo_id cover two simultaneous repositories with a colliding thread_id; test_route_identity_two_coordinator_chats_stay_disjoint covers two coordinator chats (codex vs claude) for the same repo/task/window staying disjoint in canonical form and digest.
acceptance_results.forbidden_compliance: PASS -- no task_engine_change, no process_launcher_change, no legacy_AITools_model_interface, no global_single_repo_fallback (AppServerMux/SidebandCallbackClient/CallbackBridge all fail closed on missing repo_id rather than defaulting), no manual_AIWORKHUB_REPO_ROOT_requirement introduced (new binding is AIWORKHUB_REPO_ID, set by the extension per workspace, not a manual operator step), no dangerous_mode_or_special_permission_requirement, no cross_repository_callback_delivery (this is exactly what the fix prevents), no broad_unscoped_refactor (edits confined to app_server_mux.py and callback_bridge.py plus this test/eval pair), no git_commit_or_push, no raw_broad_grep_find_tree (all code discovery via aiworkhub_worker_source_graph_query; exact-path Read only for files already located via Source Graph).

design_notes.repo_id_field: SidebandInstance gained a required repo_id: str field (no default, positioned before the defaulted fields). _read_instance_descriptor treats a missing/invalid repo_id exactly like any other malformed required field -- the whole descriptor is rejected (returns None), so a pre-B925 legacy registry row with no repo_id is excluded from ownership resolution entirely rather than silently treated as an unscoped match.
design_notes.validation: _validate_repo_id (app_server_mux.py) and the duplicated-by-design _validate_sideband_repo_id (callback_bridge.py, kept local rather than imported so this module's validation never silently depends on app_server_mux.py's internal shape) both use the bounded ASCII identifier charset [A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,128}, rejecting empty strings, whitespace, path separators (forward and back slash), non-string types, and Windows drive-letter/backslash path forms.
design_notes.fail_closed_construction: AppServerMux.__init__ requires repo_id (TypeError if omitted, ValueError if invalid). SidebandCallbackClient.__init__ requires repo_id the same way. CallbackBridge.__init__ raises ValueError when transport=="sideband" and sideband_repo_id is falsy, mirroring the existing claude_cli transport's claude_repo_id/claude_window_id fail-closed pattern (B856) rather than inventing a new convention.
design_notes.cli_entrypoint: main() resolves repo_id from AIWORKHUB_REPO_ID only for the app-server (registering) invocation shape; the non-registering execvp passthrough (`codex exec ...`) is untouched and never requires it, since it never writes to the sideband registry.
design_notes.dispatcher_wiring: CallbackDispatcher.start() now also sets kwargs.setdefault("sideband_repo_id", self.repo_id) alongside its existing claude_repo_id/claude_window_id defaults -- harmless when the resolved transport isn't "sideband" (CallbackBridge only enforces/uses it in that case), so a future switch to the sideband transport for an existing dispatcher can never silently start unbound.
design_notes.narrowed_scope: Per coordinator rework instruction, this pass touches only app_server_mux.py and callback_bridge.py (plus this test/eval pair) -- route_identity.py, repository_mux.py, callback_store.py, manager_ai_tools.py, server.py, and vscode-extension/extension.js were read for context but not modified this round.
design_notes.test_isolation: This worktree's src/aiworkhub package has no __init__.py (a namespace-package portion). Because a DIFFERENT already-importable checkout of the same package (found later on sys.path, e.g. an editable pip install of the canonical /home/shrek/GeoAI checkout) DOES have __init__.py, Python's import system treats that as the regular package and it wins over a plain sys.path.insert(0, ...) of this worktree regardless of insertion order. The test file therefore loads both app_server_mux.py and callback_bridge.py under a private top-level package name with __path__ pointed explicitly at this worktree's src/aiworkhub directory, bypassing sys.path package resolution so the exact edited source is what gets exercised. callback_bridge.py's two not-yet-ported dependencies (repository_state.py, task_store.py -- outside this task's allowed_writes, not yet present in this worktree) are stubbed via sys.modules for import purposes only; AIWORKHUB_REPO_ROOT is set before import so the module-level CALLBACK_CWD computation short-circuits on the env var and never calls into the stub.
